answer: A stake-bonded registry makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and misbehavior burns that bond. Like pigment mixed into paint, the stake is inseparable from the identity, so a Sybil attacker cannot spin up thousands of free sock-puppets at dawn and melt away like a glacier in spring - each copy costs real money, and each burned bond raises the price of the next attack.
